newsitem.title: UK: Med gasoline balanced to tight, gas oil, fuel stat.
newsitem.headline: Med gasoline balanced to tight, gas oil, fuel stat.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Tuesday, traders said.

Gasoline for the balance of June is looking balanced to tight with most prompt cargoes placed. Traders said Italy had been a good buyer through June, there was good offtake to the Far east and Romanian barrels had now be placed into Turkey.
"There is good supply of low octane material but the high octane supplies are tight," a trade with a French major said.
He said the tight market for high octane gasoline in Lavera was being further exacerbated by tight MTBE supplies after filling recent commitments to the U.S..

The lengthy low octane situation was expected to be ironed out though with Nigeria reported to be ordering the immediate importation of 33 cargoes of petroleum products to end an acute fuel shortage in the country. The cargoes were said to be coming from Europe, especially Spain as well as other African countries.

ADDAX Nigeria is reported to have bought several cargoes last week and one major refiner was seen looking to fill a large low-octane cargo out of Lavera though it was unclear whether this would be headed to Nigeria.
However, Spanish refiners said they had so far had little fresh enquiry for cargoes.
"We've had no nominations -- We bought last week for West Africa, not Nigeria and we certainly don't plan to produce anything extra for Nigeria," a trader at one major Spanish refiner said.
Traders said interest was now beginning to focus on the early requirements for Italy as well as a recent Tunisian tender for two cargoes for 8-10 July and 12-14 July arrival.
Prompt lifting cargoes were valued around fob high quotes +$1 per tonne.
Gas oil was little changed in a quietish market.

Traders said there was a fair amount of demand for low sulphur diesel into July which many thought would keep premiums above $3 for the time being. We've had a fair number of requests both from the Mediterranean and from outside the region," said one trader.
EN590 differentials were talked around quotes fob hi +$3.0.

Russian and other 0.2 percent material was generally quite subdued. Traders said the Mediterranean might get some support from arbitrage opportunities to the East although the door was not quite open yet. High sulphur cargoes seemed steady with an Italian refiner confirming it bought a 25,000-tonne cargo of bunker spec material from a French refiner at high cif Naples plus $3 on Monday.
"We paid this price at it is good material, 3 pct and we are taking it into bunkers," the buyer said.
A trader was still heard offering a large cargo of high sulphur material out of Bilbao.
"It seems the oil is there, at least in Spain," one trader said. "There are cargoes but there is demand, so cracked is quite balanced."
One percent was quiet, with one Spanish refiner heard offering.
